title: IndiGo, Air India Group to Shift Mumbai Flights to Navi Mumbai in Phases
excerpt: IndiGo will move 12 daily international departures from February 2027 and Air India Express will start Navi Mumbai services in December, as Mumbai's Terminal 1 heads for redevelopment.
body:
• IndiGo will progressively shift 12 daily international departures from Mumbai's CSMIA to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) between February and July 2027, covering Bahrain, Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah, Madinah, Kuwait, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, Muscat, Dhaka and Jakarta, plus a new daily Kathmandu service.
  • Air India Express will operate four daily domestic flights from NMIA from December 2026, add planned Kuwait services and existing Oman services from January 2027, and progressively move Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam, Doha, Muscat and Sharjah services by the Northern Summer 2027 season.
  • The moves free capacity for the phased redevelopment of CSMIA Terminal 1, whose North Section of Terminal 1B closes from January 2027 and affects about 5 million passengers a year.
  • Reader check: if you book Mumbai flights for travel from December 2026 onward, confirm whether your flight departs CSMIA (BOM) or NMIA before arranging ground transport — the two airports are in different parts of the metropolitan region.

IndiGo and the Air India Group will shift selected flights from Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) in phases over the coming months, the airlines and Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) announced on October 25. The transition is tied directly to the redevelopment of CSMIA's ageing Terminal 1.

What IndiGo is moving

According to the joint IndiGo and Adani Airports announcement reported by IANS, IndiGo will commence international services from NMIA from February 2027 and gradually shift 12 daily international departures from CSMIA. The transferred routes cover all of its present CSMIA operations to Bahrain, Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah, Madinah, Kuwait, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, Muscat, Dhaka and Jakarta. A new daily flight to Kathmandu will take IndiGo's international network at NMIA to 12 destinations between February and July 2027.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=r0CMDMwC7Cs

IndiGo will also move the domestic connectivity needed to support those international services, so passengers can connect between domestic and international flights at the new airport rather than transferring across the city. AAHL said it is building the infrastructure required for smooth domestic-to-international transfers at NMIA, describing the move as the next step in building NMIA as a long-term international hub for the carrier using its Airbus A320, A321 and A321XLR fleet.

What Air India Group is moving

Air India Group will begin its phased transition with Air India Express operating four daily domestic flights from NMIA from December 2026, according to the joint Air India Group and Adani Airports release reported by ANI. Planned services to Kuwait and existing services to Oman follow from January 2027, with Kuwait subject to approvals. The group will then progressively transition Air India Express services to Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam, Doha, Muscat and Sharjah, completing the process by the IATA Northern Summer 2027 season.

https://x.com/AdaniOnline/status/2114346293153890458

"This transition is a result of continued collaborative engagement with the airport operator and is aligned with the wider airport transition program for both Indian and international airlines and will support the long-awaited redevelopment of CSMIA Terminal 1."

— Air India Group and Adani Airports, joint release

The release said operating from both airports will preserve the historicity of the group's existing slots at CSMIA while strengthening connectivity across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.

Why Terminal 1 is closing in phases

Adani Airports will begin phased redevelopment of Terminal 1 from January 2027, starting with the North Section of Terminal 1B, citing safety concerns around the nearly 60-year-old facility, Outlook Business reported. About 5 million passengers a year — roughly 9 percent of CSMIA's total traffic of around 55 million — will be temporarily affected in the first phase, while the remaining traffic continues normally. Terminal 1 currently handles about 15 million passengers a year; redevelopment is expected to raise its capacity by 33 percent to 20 million a year, with completion targeted for 2030.

The IndiGo transfer alone accounts for around 3 million passengers, about 60 percent of the roughly 5 million passengers targeted for relocation in the first phase, according to IANS.

What this means for travellers

For diaspora travellers, the practical change is airport choice on West Asia routes. Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam, Doha, Muscat, Sharjah and Kuwait services — heavily used by Indian workers and families in the Gulf — are among the first to move. Travellers from Thane, Navi Mumbai and the eastern suburbs gain a closer airport; travellers from western Mumbai face a longer ground journey and should check departure airport carefully when booking, especially for connections.

What's next

Air India Express domestic flights start at NMIA in December 2026, the first West Asia moves follow in January and February 2027, and both airlines complete their announced transitions by the summer 2027 season. Further changes tied to the Terminal 1 redevelopment will be accommodated at CSMIA Terminal 2 where needed, the companies said.
